records.title: Introductory Topics in Marine Biology
records.header: MARBIO 197 Introductory Topics in Marine Biology (1-5, max. 10) NSc
records.text: MARBIO 197 Introductory Topics in Marine Biology (1-5, max. 10) NSc Selected topics in marine biology. Introduces the issues, principles, and methodologies required to interpret relevant data in science and social science, and to apply this knowledge to biological processes, examine human actions in the oceans, and explore solutions. Offered: AWSpS.

records.title: Aquatic Ecophysiology
records.text: MARBIO 270 Aquatic Ecophysiology (5) NSc Focuses on fundamental physiology, with an emphasis on processes relevant to living in a variety of aquatic environments. Includes a broad survey of taxa, from prokaryotes to mammals, and a variety of aquatic habitats. Prerequisite: BIOL 200. Offered: jointly with FISH 270/OCEAN 270.

records.title: Professional Development in Aquatic Sciences
records.header: MARBIO 300 Professional Development in Aquatic Sciences (2)
records.text: MARBIO 300 Professional Development in Aquatic Sciences (2) Introduces students to career opportunities in aquatic (including marine) sciences, ways to gain experience as an undergraduate such as internships and volunteering, and professional skills including developing a curriculum vitae and networking. Students learn how to align their academic activities with their career goals and to create materials that promote their professional development. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: jointly with FISH 300/OCEAN 300; A.

records.text: MARBIO 301 Current Topics in Marine Biology (1, max. 3) NSc Weekly seminar series exploring topics relating to research, communication and career pathways in Marine Biology. Promotes interdisciplinary knowledge of marine sciences, generally. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: WSp.

records.title: Conversations in Marine Biology
records.header: MARBIO 302 Conversations in Marine Biology (1) NSc
records.text: MARBIO 302 Conversations in Marine Biology (1) NSc Seminar engaging with current topics and marine biologists from a range of sectors (including academic, governmental, and the private sector) through small, student-led discussions. Co-requisite: MARBIO 301. Prerequisite: OCEAN 210; and either FISH 323, FISH 370/OCEAN 370/MARBIO 370, or OCEAN 330. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: W.

records.title: Scientific Writing in Marine Biology
records.header: MARBIO 305 Scientific Writing in Marine Biology (3)
records.text: MARBIO 305 Scientific Writing in Marine Biology (3) Introduces the fundamentals of scientific writing about research in marine biology: content, organization, critical thinking, structure, and the mechanics of grammar, wording, and formatting. Students critically evaluate scientific writing in this discipline, and practice developing, writing, and revising concise arguments supported by scientific evidence. Course overlaps with: FHL 333. Prerequisite: either C LIT 240, CMS 240, ENGL 109 and ENGL 110, ENGL 111, ENGL 121, ENGL 131, ENGL 141, ENGL 182, ENGL 197, ENGL 198, ENGL 199, ENGL 281, ENGL 282, ENGL 288, ENGL 289, ENGL 296, ENGL 297, ENGL 298, ENGL 299, HONORS 205, or HONORS 345. Offered: AWSp.

records.title: Marine Evolutionary Biology
records.text: MARBIO 370 Marine Evolutionary Biology (5) NSc Emphasizes geobiological patterns of marine evolutionary biology environment; processes of evolution; marine prokaryote and eukaryote diversity; and applications of evolutionary principles to ocean change, and conservation and management of marine biodiversity. Prerequisite: either FISH 270/OCEAN 270/MARBIO 270 or BIOL 220. Offered: jointly with FISH 370/OCEAN 370; Sp.

records.title: Marine Ecology
records.text: MARBIO 433 Marine Ecology (5) NSc Study of marine ecological processes such as recruitment, disturbance, competition, and predation, and their effects on the structure and diversity of marine communities. Weekend field trips to local intertidal habitats required. Prerequisite: either FISH 270/OCEAN 270/MARBIO 270, BIOL 356, BIOL 472, or a minimum grade of 3.4 in either BIOL 180, BIOL 240, B BIO 180, or T BIOL 120 Offered: jointly with BIOL 433.

records.title: Research in Marine Biology
records.header: MARBIO 479 Research in Marine Biology (1-15, max. 15)
records.text: MARBIO 479 Research in Marine Biology (1-15, max. 15) Individual research on topics in marine biology. Research projects supervised by an individual faculty member. records.title: Marine Biology in the Field
records.header: MARBIO 488 Marine Biology in the Field (6)
records.text: MARBIO 488 Marine Biology in the Field (6) Uses extensive field work to enhance students' practical knowledge of marine organismal and habitat diversity, and oceanographic processes. Develops integrative skills in experimental design, data collection, field interpretation, and communication. Prerequisite: OCEAN 210; either BIOL 220 or FISH 270/MARBIO 270/OCEAN 270; either MARBIO 305 or FISH 290; either Q SCI 381 or STAT 311; and either FISH 323, FISH 370/MARBIO 370/OCEAN 370, or OCEAN 330. Offered: A.
